subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should default SSRF DNS handling allow a mixed result set after removing blocked candidates, or keep rejecting the whole request when any resolved address is blocked?
rationale: The code change is small, but it relaxes a default SSRF security boundary and must reflect maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses to pinning, and test mixed plus all-blocked DNS results.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat mixed blocked DNS answers as intentionally unsafe and document trusted proxy or fake-IP opt-in paths for affected deployments.

options.title: Make it explicit opt-in
options.body: Preserve the strict default and expose or reuse a narrowly named operator-controlled policy for polluted DNS environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses to pinning, and test mixed plus all-blocked DNS results.

likelyOwner.reason: The current SSRF assertion path and nearby hardening history point here as the strongest routing candidate for the security-boundary choice.
